meaning: Each tie names the phrase of the paper that a Lean declaration states, as read side by side for Proof Reader (wcook04/proof-reader 3858afbe00b2, papers/navier-stokes-certificate-checker). Titles, reading notes, topics and comparisons are AI-drafted or AI-assessed; no mathematician has reviewed them.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).

lean.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.spaceAndTorusBreakdown_of_cell_system_condition
lean.fidelity_note: The theorem gives both whole-space and torus breakdown under the complete cell condition. This is the conditional implication stated in the opening sentence.

lean.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition
lean.fidelity_note: The condition is the fifteen-clause premise of that implication. A numerical witness satisfying it is a separate obligation.

ties.from: `CellSystemCondition` has fifteen fields over seven data arguments.
ties.to: `CellSystemCondition` has fifteen fields over seven data arguments.

lean.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition
lean.fidelity_note: The condition has fifteen direct clauses over the seven shared choices of cell data, field instances, local calculations, tree, assembly, constants and reduction data. The sentence counts these choices correctly.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange
lean.fidelity_note: Only used row coordinates are constrained by the common real row variables and complex gauge and pressure-head terms. All unused and port coordinates are free complex numbers, and both actuator blocks are required to be real.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialConditions
lean.fidelity_note: The retained potential inequality is quantified over every vector satisfying the supplied admissibility condition. In the final cell condition that is the complete compatible-row space described immediately before this sentence.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingConditions
lean.fidelity_note: The retained pairing inequality is quantified over every admissible vector. Substituting the final compatible-row condition gives the full domain stated in the passage.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationConditions
lean.fidelity_note: The residual elimination comparison is quantified over every admissible vector. It therefore includes the free and gauge directions of the full compatible-row condition.

lean.name: Breakdown.PotentialShape.VanishesBeyond
lean.fidelity_note: The missing-breakpoint default R makes each affected support guard true because R ≤ |R|. A node coefficient needs one guard and a bubble coefficient needs both endpoint guards; when both endpoints are absent, the bubble coefficient is therefore forced to zero.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetAxis.convert

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasSymmetricScale

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels
lean.fidelity_note: A label is active when it belongs to one of the four model supports and some component is nonzero at a point in the cell. The definition directly supports conservative coverage by all declared supports.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialConditions
lean.fidelity_note: The coupling-group conditions require coverage for active labels and their unresolved partners. Checking the same coverage for every declared support label is sufficient for these clauses.

lean.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowFunctionalConditions
lean.fidelity_note: The tested-row coverage condition quantifies over active model labels. It is the third consumer of the active-label set identified in the sentence.

lean.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded
lean.fidelity_note: The harmonic expansion requires the component, temporal-frequency and azimuthal-order triples to be distinct. This is the exact orthogonality requirement stated in the passage.

ties.from:
Much of the infinite and analytic content is proved in Lean, with finite data
as input: the extension of checked finite bases to infinite orthonormal ones,
spline joins and scaled-jet facts, the logarithmic radial phase, step-phase
regularity, pressure continuity and periodicity, the moved profile and adjoint
constructions, potential-series derivatives and decay, and the azimuthal dual
estimate (`AdjointDefect.remainderAzimuthalHolds_proof`).
ties.to:
Much of the infinite and analytic content is proved in Lean, with finite data
as input: the extension of checked finite bases to infinite orthonormal ones,
spline joins and scaled-jet facts, the logarithmic radial phase, step-phase
regularity, pressure continuity and periodicity, the moved profile and adjoint
constructions, potential-series derivatives and decay, and the azimuthal dual
estimate (`AdjointDefect.remainderAzimuthalHolds_proof`).

lean.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.remainderAzimuthalHolds_proof
lean.fidelity_note: The linked theorem supplies the azimuthal dual estimate by combining the angular inverse-square bound, approximation, mode pairing and time orthogonality. The earlier representation results listed in the sentence are separate results.
